subject: Math
prompt: At a company, $70%$ of employees work full-time and the remaining employees work part-time. Exactly $40%$ of full-time employees participate in the retirement plan. If exactly $31%$ of all employees at the company participate in the retirement plan, what percent of part-time employees participate in the retirement plan?
explanation: The correct answer is $10$. Since $70\%$ of employees are full-time, the remaining $30\%$ are part-time. Let $p$ represent the percent of part-time employees who participate in the retirement plan. The total percentage of employees participating equals the sum of contributions from each group: $(0.70)(0.40) + (0.30)(p/100) = 0.31$. The full-time contribution is $0.70 \times 0.40 = 0.28$, or $28\%$ of all employees. This gives $0.28 + 0.30(p/100) = 0.31$. Subtracting $0.28$ from both sides: $0.30(p/100) = 0.03$. Solving: $p/100 = 0.10$, so $p = 10$. Therefore, $10\%$ of part-time employees participate in the retirement plan.
